title: Production AI, Architecture Trade-offs & Team Design: InfoQ Opens Registration for 6 January Cohorts
gist: Promotional announcement: InfoQ opens six five-week online certification cohorts (AI Engineering, Architecture, High-Performing Teams) starting January 9-22, 2027 at USD 1,470 per person. The only substantive signal is the framing that production AI pain has shifted from model selection to retrieval, agent autonomy, evaluation and inference cost, and that AI-accelerated coding is bottlenecked by reviews, approvals and infrastructure dependencies.

insights.claim: InfoQ frames production AI engineering as dominated by decisions beyond model selection: context retrieval and maintenance, how much autonomy to give agents, and managing reliability, latency and inference costs.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Value in enterprise AI stacks is accruing to retrieval, agent orchestration, evaluation and inference-cost tooling rather than model choice alone; watch vendors in those layers.
insights.quote: Production AI involves decisions beyond model selection: how context is retrieved and maintained, how much autonomy agents should have, and how reliability, latency, and inference costs are managed.
insights.locator: AI Engineering: Retrieval, Agents, and Evaluation

insights.claim: A Rabobank principal engineer's QCon London 2026 talk examined a production RAG system built on more than 10,000 documents and used by more than 300 people, illustrating the typical scale of internal bank RAG deployments.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Enterprise RAG in regulated finance is in production but at modest internal scale (hundreds of users), suggesting early-stage adoption depth.
insights.quote: a production RAG system built on more than 10,000 documents and used by more than 300 people

insights.claim: Faster AI-assisted coding does not necessarily improve software delivery when code reviews, approvals or infrastructure dependencies become the binding constraint.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Productivity gains from AI coding tools may be capped by downstream review/CI/approval capacity, favoring tooling that addresses review and delivery flow.
insights.quote: Faster coding does not necessarily improve delivery when reviews, approvals, or infrastructure dependencies become the constraint.
insights.locator: High-Performing Teams: Delivery Flow, Ownership, and AI

insights.claim: AI agents are changing how engineering responsibilities are divided and which work still requires human judgment, prompting InfoQ to treat team structure, ownership, delivery flow, AI responsibilities and engineering metrics as a single operating model.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Engineering organizations are redesigning operating models around agents, a demand signal for engineering-metrics and workflow platforms.
insights.quote: AI agents also change how responsibilities are divided and which work requires human judgment.
insights.locator: High-Performing Teams: Delivery Flow, Ownership, and AI

insights.claim: InfoQ is running six five-week online certification cohorts starting January 9-22, 2027 across AI Engineering (three cohorts), Architecture (two) and High-Performing Teams (one), priced at USD 1,470 per person with four hours of live sessions per week.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Half the cohorts are AI engineering, indicating where paid practitioner training demand is concentrated.

insights.claim: InfoQ's Architect Program capstone has participants co-author a technical article on AI's role in software architecture or platform engineering, with selected pieces potentially published on InfoQ.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Minor: InfoQ is using cohorts as a content pipeline on AI architecture.
insights.locator: The capstone involves co-authoring a technical article
